name: newlisp
why: A small Lisp-family scripting language with its own quirks and a lovely, obscure character, rarely seen today.

brief.what_it_is: newlisp is a Lisp-like, general-purpose scripting language, according to its Homebrew formula description. The formula installs three executables: newlisp, newlisp-10.7.5 (a version-suffixed copy), and newlispdoc. I could not read the project's homepage or README, so I have no details on its syntax, feature set, or what input and output look like in practice. The scout's note calls it a small Lisp-family language with its own quirks.
brief.install_notes: Installed via Homebrew. The formula's caveats say that if brew is installed under a custom prefix, the included examples need to be pointed at your newlisp executable. I could not check anything beyond that from the README.
brief.standout: The scout describes it as having a lovely, obscure character and being rarely seen today. I could not confirm this from the project's own pages, so treat it as the scout's impression rather than something I verified.
brief.caveats: The homepage https://www.newlisp.org/ was unreachable. Both the https and http forms failed with URLError, so this brief rests only on the Homebrew formula metadata and the scout notes. No README, release date, or commit history was available, so I could not judge whether the project is maintained.
